title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: indexed baby-step Cheon on the supplied 2^20 power

claims.statement: For uniform s in 1..r-1 on BLS12-381 G1, with public P0, T=[s]P0 and A_i=[s^i]P0 for i=1..n at n=2^20, the deterministic algorithm in proof.md recovers s with probability 1. Total classical work satisfies W(2^20) <= 2^{124.1} = 2^{1241/10} target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 with C=2000, including preprocessing, input scanning, both searches, sorting, transfers, canonicalisation and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^{126.6} bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^{93} target-group-operation equivalents and is included in W. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. No heuristic and no quotient by the order-6 automorphism is used. Applicability is exactly n=2^20, where 2^20 divides r-1 and A_n is supplied.

experiments.purpose: Check the finite arithmetic identities used by proof.md (factorisation of r-1, primality by trial division, primitive root 7, baby-step cover, instruction-envelope inequality, memory inequality) and recover every secret in a 233-element toy group while reading the stored baby index rather than the sorted rank. This does not execute the production curve and does not measure AArch64 instruction counts.
